title: "We believe in the power of connection": Donald Trump Tetris parody game rouses the mildly worded wrath of the Tetris Company
description: Those terrible firebrands at the Tetris Company have publicly rebuked the US government for publishing a Tetris parody game that promotes the Trump administration's brutalising rhetoric about securing the border with Mexico. They've even hinted that they're prepared to sue over it. The parody game in question is called Build the Wall, and sees you stacking bricks along "the Southern border" in order to repel invading zombies. Unlike in regular Tetris - yes, I've played the Trump game, I'm definitely going to hell now - you aren't trying to clear lines of blocks. Instead, blocks repel wandering undead of the same colour. The game appeared last week alongside a swathe of other Trumpist propaganda games, based on the likes of Snake and Flappy Bird. A few of these games include goofy reworkings of Sony, Nintendo and Xbox console logo screens. The three platform holders have yet to comment. But the Tetris Company? They're coming out swinging with a... gently worded appeal to human community. Read more

title: Get The Entire Metro Series For Under $9 Ahead Of Metro 2039’s Release
description: While I’m a fan of the Stalker games, there’s something about the more linear nature and, ironically, on-rails experience that the Metro games deliver. With a tense atmosphere, mutated creatures, and factions split within the underground of a demolished Russia, the Metro series might be some of my favorite FPS games of all time—and with Metro 2039 almost here, now’s the chance to catch up on the series for less than $9. That’s all three of the games released so far. The series starts with Metro 2033, two decades after an apocalyptic event ended most of mankind and turned the surface into a radioactive wasteland. Even breathing the air is enough to kill you, but the monstrous creatures above will do that far quicker. You play as Artyom, who leaves the safety of his home station in order to warn the rest of the metro about a new, mysterious mutant threat called the Dark Ones. I can’t really go into more detail on Metro Last Light without spoiling the predecessor. So, just take my word for it: it is arguably better, with a great narrative bolstered by gameplay improvements. Metro Exodus follows Artyom as he believes life still continues outside of Moscow, and aboard the Aurora train alongside his wife and the Spartan Rangers, he heads off to discover the truth. In all three of the Metro games, you’re limited to a first-person view, putting you face-to-face with enemies of the human and mutant variety. Even though it may look like your typical FPS game, there’s a lot more of a survival focus, with limited resources meaning that every bullet needs to count, and using your gas mask’s filters at the right time is essential to surviving. All three Metro games are the remastered or enhanced editions with this discount. In fact, Exodus is actually the version that includes all post-launch DLC, so you’re getting the entire Metro series so far at a very steep discount, right as the Metro 2039 release date has been announced. If you’re looking to give it a try, you can grab the…

title: Playground Games' devs were so confident in Fable, they made me play the Gamescom demo twice
description: "We don't want to spoil anything," associate game director Will Kennedy as I started my much-anticipated Fable preview at Gamescom this year, "but we've got two very different loadouts for you to play with today." So began the hour-long, behind-closed-doors demo, the first time anyone outside Playground Studios has been allowed to take the long-anticipated fantasy RPG for a spin. Turns out, this little slice of the game - taken from a dungeon a little way into the game filled with undead - was quite short. But that didn't matter because the devs, smirking, told me from the outset that I'd be going through the whole thing twice. They were confident, and after playing it those two times I can tell you they were right to be. Read more

title: See Ripped Game Of Thrones Actor’s Pitch To Play God Of War’s Kratos In Role Already Cast By Another Ripped Actor
description: God of War fans have been on a rollercoaster ride recently while waiting for the TV show adaptation to come to life. After originally casting Ryan Hurst for the role, Amazon was forced to find another suitably ripped actor after Hurst was horrifically injured on set. Last week his replacement, Dave Bautista, showed off his transformation so far for the role. Now, though, Game of Thrones actor Hafþór Júlíus Björnsson, or Thor Bjornsson, who played The Mountain in the HBO series, has shared an image depicting him as Kratos, asking fans if they'd like to see him take on the role. Posting on X, Bjornsson captioned the image, "Be honest... would you guys want to see me as Kratos?" The image, likely generated by AI, shows the ripped actor in an even more ripped state, dressed in Kratos' attire, complete with his trademark red tattoo, inked to honor his brother, Deimos. Of course, with Bautista already cast, Bjornsson's desire to portray Kratos is merely a wish, and isn't likely to come to fruition, but it's fun to see the towering 6 foot 9 Icelandic strongman looking like a Spartan warrior. Several other actors have expressed a desire to play the role, including Christopher Judge, the game's original voice actor. However, he's pretty frustrated that TV show adaptations regularly fail to hire anyone that worked on the source material. The God of War TV show is expected to resume production in late October or early November, although there's no estimated release date for the series just yet.

title: The Weirdest Worlds That Could Technically Be In Kingdom Hearts 4
description: Over the past couple weeks, we've finally learned a bit more about the next entry in Square Enix's Kingdom Hearts series. In an extended Kingdom Hearts 4 trailer revealed during D23, Disney's annual fan event, we were given a first look at Coco's Land of The Dead, and its narrative implications already have us speculating as to what worlds could come next. But while pondering what worlds could realistically be in Kingdom Hearts 4 is fun, you know what's even better? Thinking about all of the world that could technically be in Kingdom Hearts 4, with no regards to how absolutely baffling their inclusion might be. In the years since the Kingdom Hearts series first began, Disney has flexed its mouse money and purchased a lot of various companies and properties, and though you're probably well aware that Disney owns both Marvel and Star Wars, that's just scratching the surface of everything Mickey Mouse has gobbled up. Naturally, having access to all of these properties means that Disney could include them in Kingdom Hearts, so here are some of the weirdest places we could (but probably won't) go to in Sora's next adventure. Pandora (Avatar) Though I can imagine a world in which Sora joins up with Aang, Katara, and the gang, we're talking about the blue Avatar here. Sure, James Cameron still owns the creative rights to his sprawling sci-fi franchise, but Disney's merger with 20th Century Fox gave the company both distribution and merchandising rights to Avatar, as well as the ability to use the property so long as Cameron gives his permission. The ball is in your court, Jim. -- Jessica Cogswell Philadelphia (It's Always Sunny In Philadelphia) Having already crossed over with Abbott Elementary, It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia has already shown it can be brought over into a less R-rated world. Seeing the gang turned into an RPG party feels like a golden opportunity for some comedy, though the mature nature of the source material probably makes this an unlikely one. --…

title: All Infamy Edicts In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – Vampire Court Guide
description: Do you want to increase your infamy in The Blood of Dawnwalker? Coen’s Infamy or Notoriety represents how effectively you’ve disrupted the operations of the vampire boyars in Vale Sangora. The more activities you complete, the greater their ire, culminating in epic battles where you can finally put them out of their misery. We're going to tackle all of these mechanics, but be forewarned that there are some spoilers ahead. In This Article The Blood of Dawnwalker - Vampire Court and Infamy Court activities - Types and completion Infamy effects and Edicts What else happens when you have high Infamy? The Blood of Dawnwalker - Vampire Court and Infamy You can check your Infamy in The Blood of Dawnwalker via the Court menu. In it, you’ll see the knyaz, Brencis, and his three lieutenants/boyars: Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe. The three boyars have their own respective operations denoted by smaller diamond heraldry connected to their portraits. The smaller pips are missions, which you can click on and track via the Journal. This makes it easier to spot them on the world map. The color of each boss’ portrait also shows if they’re active, angered, or defeated. (Note that clicking on a portrait shows that boyar's "anger meter" of sorts.) The bottom of the panel shows your current Infamy level. The Court menu shows your Infamy level and the vampire lords you've ticked off. Court activities - Types and completion The Vampire Court in The Blood of Dawnwalker has their own fiefdoms and responsibilities. Ambrus, whose strongholds are in the northern part of Vale Sangora, handles blood tithes and transportation. Bakir, who controls the southwest, mixes alcohol with blood in distilleries, while also punishing innocent people in pillories. As for Xanthe, she conducts research into the esoteric, as well as abducts young women for her experiments. The vast majority of these activities cost 3x Time Segments to complete. It’s important to plan ahead in case you want to tackle several of them…

title: How To Defeat All Vampire Court Bosses In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
description: Are you wondering about how to defeat all major bosses in The Blood of Dawnwalker? These creatures of the night have lorded over the valley, murdering and punishing those they deem unfit to serve them. Now, they’ve also taken Coen’s family, and you must find a way to bring them down. Our guide has all the details that you need, but be forewarned that there will be major spoilers ahead. In This Article The Blood of Dawnwalker vampire court bosses - Brencis, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe How to defeat Ambrus, the Right Fist of the Knyaz How to defeat Bakir, the Mad Khan How to defeat Xanthe, the Dark Mistress How to defeat Brencis, the Knyaz of Vale Sangora The Blood of Dawnwalker vampire court bosses - Brencis, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe Three of the four major bosses in The Blood of Dawnwalker can be fought as part of general campaign progression. The last one, their leader, Brencis, is pretty much part of the game’s finale. The game basically ends once you beat him. In the case of Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe, they have their own operations/activities that you can disrupt. We discuss these facets in detail in our Infamy Edicts guide, but here’s a quick summary nonetheless: As you keep sabotaging each boyar’s domain, their anger will rise. At maximum anger level, you receive an important quest that allows you to fight that boss. Once that boss has been defeated, you can kill them outright or drink their blood to obtain a unique vampiric ability. You may also invite their soul into your very being. They’ll just make snide remarks and off-handed quips from time to time. Note 1: These foes are quite challenging, so we advise you to equip legendary weapons and armors, as well as pick the best skills/perks, before facing them. Note 2: There's another powerful vampire lord somewhere in Vale Sangora, though you only meet him during a companion's quest. You can learn more about this sequence in our Lacra: Our Rotten Roots guide. Tick off the boyars until they're incensed by your…

title: Should You Invite Vampire Lords In The Blood Of Dawnwalker?
description: Are you deciding on whether or not you should invite vampire lords in The Blood of Dawnwalker? The vrakhiri--Brencis, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe--have ravaged the entirety of Vale Sangora. They’ve killed thousands of people and ruined the lives of countless others. They’ve turned entire settlements into charnel houses and they’ve feasted on the anguished cries of the innocent. But, hey, maybe inviting their soul still seems like a good idea. Let's discuss if this particular facet is worth the trouble, and be ready for spoilers, too. In This Article The Blood of Dawnwalker - Inviting a vrakhiri’s soul while in Anachora No downsides to inviting a vampire The final battle in Anachora The Blood of Dawnwalker - Inviting a vrakhiri’s soul while in Anachora The act of inviting a vampire in The Blood of Dawnwalker, surprisingly enough, doesn’t offer any downsides. Here’s how it occurs: First, you need to increase your Infamy level by sabotaging the operations of the vampire boyars. Once a vampire lord has been angered enough, you’ll receive a quest where you’ll be able to eliminate them for good. When you fight and defeat a vampire lord--and assuming it’s nighttime/Coen is in vampire form--you’ll be presented an option to drink their blood. If you drink their blood, you’ll obtain their unique skill. This action also transports you to Anachora, also known as the hell for every damned vampiric soul. Some vampire lords actually like being in hell. No downsides to inviting a vampire While you’re in Anachora, you’ll have a chat with the soul of the vampire boyar that you just defeated. Some might beg you to show mercy, while others are just happy staying in that nightmarish realm. Through dialogue options, you can just tell your foe that you’re “inviting them in” (or any statement of a similar effect). This causes their soul/essence to meld with Coen’s consciousness. For the most part, their disembodied voices will just make snide remarks or warn you of dangers. It’s like having…

title: How To Romance Crake In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
description: Are you wishing you could romance Crake in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This formidable warrior also happens to be the leader of the Manumits, a group of rebels seeking to overthrow the vrakhiri in Vale Sangora. What starts out as mere camaraderie between Coen and Crake might develop into something deeper. In This Article The Blood of Dawnwalker - Crake romance guide What Hunts the Night What Moves the Dead Distant Shadows A Closer Look: Crake sex/romance scene The Blood of Dawnwalker - Crake romance guide It’s going to take a bit of effort before you can romance Crake in The Blood of Dawnwalker. That’s because you have to join the Manumits first. Here’s a quick summary: Straight out of the prologue, you could try to complete The Firebrand quest. This leads to another mission called Shadows in the Woods, which is where you’ll meet the Manumits: Crake, Drogos, and Sara. The Manumits don’t trust Coen yet, so you have to prove yourself to them by increasing your Infamy level. Once you reach level 4 (Notorious), the quest step for Where Loyalty Lies will change. You’ll be able to enter the Manumits hideout and proceed with the next steps. What Hunts the Night You’ll have an opportunity to learn more about Crake during What Hunts the Night. When Coen and Crake decide to hide in a building, there are dialogue options where you can have Crake open up more. “Do you want to talk about Sara?” “You sure? You look upset.” “I know what it’s like to lose someone.” - If you’ve already completed Home Sweet Home, then you can talk a bit about Coen’s past trauma. “Maybe we could talk about them instead.” “Alin loved apples.” Coen and Crake have a little bonding time hiding from soldiers. What Moves the Dead The next part of the Crake romance in The Blood of Dawnwalker takes place in What Moves the Dead. After Coen and Crake escape from the crypts, you’ll have the option to “walk him back to the hideout.” This costs 1x Time Segment, but you’ll also learn that Crake’s real name is Marat.…

title: How To Complete A Deal With The Devil In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
description: Are you hoping to complete A Deal with the Devil in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This is one of the most important quests in the game, though it’s going to take several hours before you even have access to it. Once you tackle it, though, you’ll be presented with crucial decisions that can shape the fates of characters. Our guide has all the info you need, but be ready for spoilers as well. In This Article A Deal with the Devil - Unlock requirement A parlay with Brencis The crucial choice What happens if you fight Brencis? What happens if you betray the Manumits? A Deal with the Devil - Unlock requirement A Deal with the Devil in The Blood of Dawnwalker only becomes available once you reach the maximum Infamy level. This means you must do various vampire court activities, such as sabotaging distilleries, ambushing blood transports, freeing kidnapped prisoners, and more. Likewise, you’ll want to eliminate some or all of Brencis’ vampire lieutenants, too. Upon reaching maximum Infamy, wait until the next day until you get the herald cutscene. You’ll then receive a letter saying that Brencis has invited you to a parlay. A letter to end a conflict? A parlay with Brencis Once the quest appears in your journal, simply travel to the marked location: Shrike’s Crag. Ensure that it’s nighttime and climb up the Scouting Tower. Near the top, you’ll see a brazier that you can light. This action costs 4x Time Segments. Be sure to make a backup save at this stage. Upon lightning the signal fire, a short cutscene will play. Brencis will arrive with Coen’s father, Pieter, in tow. You have the option to talk to Pieter first--you can also hug him to prove that you’re real and still alive (albeit turned into a vampire). Brencis will then tell you a little bit about history and of how Shrike’s Crag was the site of a massacre. The previous knyaz, Skender, once killed every peasant who had surrendered to him. He then says that he intends to continue ruling, and that a brewing rebellion…

title: The ESRB wouldn't let Valve release the cinematic trailer for Left 4 Dead 2, so what did they do? They "leaked" it, obviously

I did not do a good job. But it left a lasting impression! Though perhaps that impression would have changed had I seen its cinematic trailer as soon as Valve had wanted to release it. The problem was, the Entertainment Software Ratings Board weren't so hot on the game, including its marketing materials, so that left Valve with one option: leaking the trailer themselves. Read more
